excluded_dates.reason: forecast orbit (least accurate geolocation); waiting for the reprocessed product

hypotheses.name: Ice or snow melt and refreeze
hypotheses.why: Meltwater makes ice dark to radar; refreezing makes it bright again.
supporting: HH changed by 2 dB or more
date falls in the melt season
not_seen: the change reversed (refroze or melted back)
would_confirm: MODIS or Landsat snow/ice image of the same week
Air temperature records above freezing

hypotheses.name: Vegetation loss (clearing, burn or scar)
hypotheses.why: Losing canopy removes volume scattering, so HV drops.
supporting: interferometric coherence increased (bare ground is more stable)
not_seen: the area was vegetated
cannot_test: HV dropped by 2 dB or more
would_confirm: Optical image shows bare soil or burn scar
A field photo of the cleared area

hypotheses.name: Fresh lava or volcanic surface change
hypotheses.why: New lava changes surface roughness: rough a'a flows brighten radar, smooth pahoehoe darkens it.
supporting: HH changed by 3 dB or more
the change persisted (lava does not wash away)
not_seen: bare or sparsely vegetated ground
cannot_test: the ground is also moving 5 mm or more per 12 days
would_confirm: Volcano observatory eruption and lava-flow maps (e.g. USGS HVO)
Thermal satellite imagery of the same dates

hypotheses.name: New structure or debris pile
hypotheses.why: Walls and piles create a strong double bounce: HH and HV both rise.
not_seen: HH rose by 2 dB or more
a road is within 300 m
would_confirm: Optical image shows new buildings or material
Local construction records

hypotheses.name: Wet snow
hypotheses.why: Liquid water in snow absorbs radar: both channels drop.
not_seen: date is in the cold season
would_confirm: Optical snow cover image (e.g. MODIS snow)
Weather station temperature

hypotheses.name: Open water / flooding
hypotheses.why: Smooth water reflects radar away, so both channels drop sharply.
supporting: HH dropped by 3 dB or more
not_seen: a river or stream is within 1 km
more than 100 mm of rain in the 30 days before
contradicting: no river, wetland or water body within 1 km to supply the water
cannot_test: HV dropped by 3 dB or more
would_confirm: An optical image (e.g. NASA HLS) from the same week shows water
Backscatter returns to its old level on a later pass as water recedes

hypotheses.name: Flooding under vegetation
hypotheses.why: Water under a canopy creates a strong double bounce, so HH rises.
not_seen: HH rose by 3 dB or more
the area is forest, shrub, wetland or mangrove
a river is within 1 km
the change reversed later (water receded)
would_confirm: Field report or optical image of standing water under trees

hypotheses.name: Landslide or debris flow
hypotheses.why: Fresh debris replaces vegetation and changes surface roughness.
supporting: HH changed by 1.5 dB or more (roughness changed)
not_seen: slope is 20° or steeper
coherence dropped (surface disturbed)
150 mm or more of rain in the 30 days before
contradicting: terrain is too flat for a landslide
would_confirm: Deposit downslope or in the river channel
Road blockage or damage reports
Field photos of the scarp

hypotheses.name: Seasonal wetland inundation
hypotheses.why: Wetlands fill and drain with the seasons; open water darkens, flooded vegetation brightens.
supporting: HH changed by 2 dB or more
not_seen: mapped as wetland, mangrove or water
the change reversed with the season
rain in the 30 days before
contradicting: not mapped as wetland or water
would_confirm: Water level gauge or optical image
The same rhythm in other years

hypotheses.name: Crop growth (canopy filling in)
hypotheses.why: As crops grow, leaves and stalks scatter radar inside the canopy, so HV rises faster than HH.
supporting: date falls in the growing season
not_seen: mapped as cropland or grassland
cannot_test: HV rose by 2 dB or more
would_confirm: Optical image showing the crop canopy (e.g. NASA HLS)
Local planting and crop calendar

hypotheses.name: Slow ground movement
hypotheses.why: Radar phase measures centimetre-scale motion along the line of sight.
not_seen: on a slope
cannot_test: moving 5 mm or more per 12 days along the line of sight
the motion has the same sign over 3+ pairs
both orbit directions see it: mostly None motion
some pairs jump by about one phase cycle (119 mm): unwrapping errors, removed from the rate
would_confirm: The same motion seen from the other orbit direction
GNSS station or crack monitoring on the ground

hypotheses.name: Processing artifact or one-off error
hypotheses.why: A single image can be misaligned or processed differently; real change should repeat on later passes.
not_seen: seen only on the latest image, with no later pass to confirm it
an extreme drop or rise of 8 dB or more in every channel
very steep slope, where small misalignments look like change
the slope faces the radar steeply (layover), where geometry distorts brightness
contradicting: the change persisted over at least two later images
would_confirm: The same change on the next NISAR pass (see the next expected pass date)
The same change in the reprocessed, precise-orbit version of this image

hypotheses.name: Crop harvest or ploughing
hypotheses.why: Harvest removes the crop canopy, a seasonal drop in HV.
not_seen: the area is mapped as cropland
the date falls in a common harvest season
would_confirm: Local crop calendar
Optical image showing harvested fields

hypotheses.name: Soil moisture after rain
hypotheses.why: Wet soil reflects more radar energy, so HH rises across the area.
not_seen: HH rose moderately
rain in the 30 days before
the surroundings changed in the same way
the change reversed later (soil dried)
contradicting: the change is local, unlike the surroundings
cannot_test: HV rose more than HH: that is vegetation volume growing, not soil getting wetter
would_confirm: Rain gauge record
Backscatter falls back once soils dry

priority.note: Monitoring priority, not a hazard prediction. Weights are shown so anyone can question them.

motion.convention: Line-of-sight change relative to the median of this window. Ionosphere screen removed; troposphere not corrected. Check the GUNW product specification for the sign convention.

motion2d.note: Size and vertical/east-west split are reliable; whether vertical motion is up or down is not confirmed, because NISAR's product specification does not state the phase sign convention.

validation.method: Gamma likelihood-ratio change-point test with Conradsen (2016) omnibus gate; HH and HV combined with a Satterthwaite correction for their measured correlation
validation.note: Simulated speckle from correlated complex-Gaussian looks (HH-HV coherence 0 to 0.9), not real NISAR labels.
